correctness.rationale: The 24 square/triangle edges give eight silhouette candidates in each coordinate family, and a projected edge occurs precisely when its outward facet normals have opposite viewing signs. Generic silhouette size is six or eight; the eight-edge event is the weighted triangle-inequality failure. Spherical-lune angle probability delta/pi gives E[H]=8/pi sum_i arccos((1/a_i)/sqrt(sum_j a_j^-2)); solving E[H]=6+2P8 proves the asserted law. For t_i=r_i^2, maximizing F=sum arcsin sqrt(t_i) over the closed simplex has boundary F=pi/2 and the sole interior critical point t_i=1/3, giving sharp rigid minimum. A continuous path toward the simplex boundary gives the unattained maximum P8->1. Independent direction-sampling at regular, (1,2,3), and (1,1,10) stretches corroborated the analytic values; random finite directions are not the proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The prior polytope is a six-vertex octahedron or a different cube–octahedron truncation parameter, not arbitrary coordinate stretches of the 12-vertex cuboctahedron. Neither dominates this axis-family theorem.
